open.description: Secret ownership does not propagate through the arithmetic itself; the P-256 engine keeps fixed-width storage but the transfer window into and out of it remains open.
The constant-time inversion's scratch storage and the operands' normalised limb-count metadata remain the recorded residual.
The ECDSA per-signature allocation count falls from 273.4 to 253.6 against 29 for the authority; it is improved, not discharged.
The candidate was built from an uncommitted worktree at 2004ea243; the changed-path digest and DSO digest are recorded, but the candidate is not reproducible from a commit.

The binary branch audit covers the P-256 mont_reduce_into and wide_mul_x86 kernels (8 of 9 targets resolve) but exits 1 because mod_exp_core_consttime_from_parts is inlined out of this DSO; the post-fix re-run at 83f67826 still exits 1 with the same 8 of 9, so there is no passing audit at any candidate digest.
The in-crate differential courts pass, but they link the crate and are bound to the source tree, not to the distribution DSO digest.
The venue exposes no PMU and has no frequency, turbo, SMT or isolation control; every row is SCOPED_OBSERVATION.
ctgrind executed the debug test binary built from the same source, not the distribution DSO; its context count is not a DSO-level result.

Post-fix: the release branch at p256.rs:690 is removed and the post-fix minimal population (DSO 83f67826) has 0 engine origin contexts, but the write-back store_coordinate (ec/smpl.rs:2624) -> limbs::normalise (bn/limbs.rs:42) still branches on the secret top limb. It cannot be stored at fixed width inside this item without breaking the no-trailing-zero-limb BIGNUM invariant the exported representation relies on.

Post-fix: no timing measurement is bound to the post-fix DSO 83f67826; the recorded 18.69x ecdsa256 row is the pre-fix digest. The release mutation-control rebuild aborted on LLVM allocation under the court's RLIMIT_DATA (evidence/incidents/2026-11-25-4).

threat_model.observation_model: wall-clock latency on a virtualised host; no PMU, no cache or branch counters, no frequency, turbo or SMT control
threat_model.statement: P-256 private scalars and ECDSA nonces are SECRET_DATA; the field prime, the group order and the base point are public. The P-256 field engine uses masked add, subtract, select, cswap and conditional subtraction with fixed loop counts; neither its selection nor its loop bounds read a value. ctgrind at the same source records no new context, but that is bounded evidence, not a constant-time proof.
